TenantId.description: The owning tenant. docs/plan/06 § The hierarchy. Hyphenated 'D' form; braced, parenthesised and bare-hex forms are rejected so that one resource has exactly one path.

CyberCloud.Analytics.clickhouseClusters.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Analytics/clickhouseClusters. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the cluster is billed in.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose namespace holds the ClickHouse cluster.

keeperNodes.description: Number of ClickHouse Keeper nodes. Keeper is a Raft quorum, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one and an even count tolerates no more failures than the odd count below it. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all.

enabled.description: Whether ClickHouse's own Prometheus endpoint is served on port 9363. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ It makes the metrics exist; the object that scrapes them is not built — see conformance.yaml § owed.

replicas.description: Number of replicas per shard. This is the availability axis, and it only applies to tables the tenant creates as Replicated — the resource does not manage tables. Total server count is shards times replicas.

shards.description: Number of shards. This is the capacity and parallelism axis: a table's data is split across shards and a query fans out to all of them. ⚠ Resharding an existing table is not something the operator or this resource does, so growing this moves new data only.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per ClickHouse server, either by preset or explicitly. The Keeper nodes are sized by the platform and are not affected.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 8Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Analytics uses the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB.

storage.description: The data volume, per ClickHouse server.

class.description: StorageClass name for the ClickHouse servers and the Keeper nodes. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: Data volume size per ClickHouse server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

version.description: ClickHouse version, which is also the ClickHouse Keeper version — the two share a release train and a wire protocol. Only long-term-support lines are offered; a new api-version is what adds a third.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Cache.redis.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Cache/redis. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the cache is billed in.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose namespace holds the RedisFailover.

maxmemoryPolicy.description: What happens when the cache reaches its memory limit. noeviction returns an error to the writer rather than dropping a key somebody is relying on.

mode.description: Replication topology. Sentinel is the only one this operator implements, and a client written against it is not portable to a sharded deployment, so it may not change after create.

enabled.description: Whether the operator runs a metrics exporter beside every Valkey and every Sentinel pod.

persistence.description: What survives a restart. None of the three settings makes a cache a database.

class.description: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

fsync.description: How often the append-only file reaches the disk. Read only when the mode is AOF; everysec can lose the last second of writes.

mode.description: None keeps nothing, RDB snapshots periodically, AOF appends every write.

size.description: Persistent volume size in Kubernetes quantity form. Unused when the mode is None, which keeps the data directory in memory.

replicas.description: Number of Valkey instances, including the primary. One is a single point of failure and is offered for development only.

sizing.description: CPU and memory, either by preset or explicitly.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset. It also sets maxmemory, so a cache evicts or refuses before the kernel kills the pod.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Caches use the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB.

version.description: Major Valkey version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

masterName.description: The Sentinel master group to ask for. Every client library takes this as a separate argument from the host.

password.description: The requirepass value, read from the tenant's Vault for this call only.

CyberCloud.ContainerService.managedClust.description: The body of a CyberCloud.ContainerService/managedClusters. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the cluster is billed in.

clusterId.description: The management cluster the control plane runs in. ⚠ This is not the cluster being created: it is the cluster whose API server accepts the Cluster API objects that create one.

controlPlane.description: The control plane, which runs as pods in the management cluster.

replicas.description: How many copies of the API server, controller manager and scheduler to run. Two survives a node failure; one is offered for development. ⚠ Unlike an etcd quorum this is a plain replica count — the datastore is separate and is shared — so an even number is not the mistake it would be on a Raft member set.

enabled.description: Whether the control plane's own metrics endpoints are scraped. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ It covers the control plane, which runs in the management cluster. Nothing scrapes inside the cluster being created; that needs an agent in the bundle.

network.description: The address space of the cluster being created.

podCidr.description: The CIDR block pods are addressed from. ⚠ It must not overlap the management cluster's own pod or service range, and nothing checks that — an overlap produces a cluster whose nodes route the platform's addresses to themselves.

serviceCidr.description: The CIDR block Service cluster IPs are allocated from. The same overlap warning applies.

version.description: The Kubernetes minor version of the control plane. The patch level is the platform's. ⚠ Upgrade the control plane before the node pools and by at most one minor at a time; a node pool may run up to three minors behind and may never run ahead. Neither rule is enforced by this API today — an illegal pair is refused by the cluster's own admission, after the create was accepted.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.ContainerService.managedClust.title: CyberCloud.ContainerService/managedClusters

CyberCloud.ContainerService.managedClust.description: What CyberCloud.ContainerService/managedClusters/listCredentials returns. ⚠ Secret material. docs/plan/08 § The provider registry makes a secret action the only path a secret value leaves by; this schema is therefore the complete list of what does.

apiServerEndpoint.description: The URL the kubeconfig points at, https://host:port. ⚠ It is an address inside the management cluster and is not routable from anywhere else — the control plane is deliberately not exposed, because there is no upstream field to attach a CIDR allow-list to. Returned separately so that a caller does not have to parse YAML to discover that.

expiresAt.description: When the credential stops working, RFC 3339. ⚠ Returned because a credential with no stated expiry is one every caller will paste into CI and never rotate — docs/plan/13 makes "a kubectl credential that expires" part of what a tenant is buying.

kubeconfig.description: A complete kubeconfig for the cluster, YAML. ⚠ docs/plan/13 requires this to be short-lived and scoped rather than the cluster's admin credential; what Cluster API generates is the admin one, and narrowing it needs a certificate request against the cluster this platform cannot yet reach.

CyberCloud.ContainerService.managedClust.description: The body of a CyberCloud.ContainerService/managedClusters/agentPools. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the pool is billed in.

autoscale.description: Whether a cluster-autoscaler may resize the pool.

enabled.description: Whether the pool carries autoscaler bounds. Off by default. ⚠ Turning it on changes what the pool costs: quota is then reserved against maxCount, because a pool that may grow to twenty machines has to have twenty machines' worth of headroom to grow into.

maxCount.description: The largest the autoscaler may grow the pool to, and what quota is reserved against while autoscaling is on. ⚠ Nothing checks that it is at least minCount — that is a relation between two properties of one body, which the schema validates nothing about.

minCount.description: The smallest the autoscaler may shrink the pool to. Ignored when autoscaling is off.

clusterId.description: The management cluster the machine objects are applied to. Must be the one the cluster is in — nothing checks that, and a pool placed elsewhere produces a MachineDeployment naming a Cluster that is not there, which Cluster API accepts and never reconciles.

count.description: How many worker VMs the pool runs. ⚠ When autoscaling is on this is the starting size and the autoscaler moves it; quota is reserved against the maximum in that case, not against this.

osDiskSize.description: The root volume of each VM, in Kubernetes quantity form. It holds the operating system, the container images and every writable layer, so a pool running large images needs more of it than a pool running small ones.

size.description: The VM size, from the platform's sizing catalogue. Kubernetes nodes use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB. ⚠ Immutable: a Cluster API machine template cannot be resized in place, so changing this would mean replacing every VM in the pool, which is a different operation from the one a PUT looks like.

upgrade.description: How machines are replaced when the pool changes.

maxSurge.description: How many extra machines may exist during a rolling replacement. One means a new VM boots and joins before an old one is removed, which is why it is the default: it costs one machine's capacity and loses none.

maxUnavailable.description: How many machines may be missing during a rolling replacement. Zero with a surge of one is the safe pair; raising it is faster and reduces the pool's capacity while it runs. ⚠ Both being zero would make an upgrade unable to start, and nothing refuses that pair.

version.description: The Kubernetes minor version the nodes run. ⚠ It may be up to three minors behind the cluster's control plane and may never be ahead of it. This API does not check that — the cluster's version is a different resource — so an illegal pair is accepted here and produces nodes that join and then misbehave.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.ContainerService.managedClust.title: CyberCloud.ContainerService/managedClusters/agentPools

storage.description: The data volume. Every instance gets its own.

size.description: Data volume size in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

version.description: Major MariaDB version, by LTS series. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window.

location.description: The region the server is billed in.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

class.description: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

CyberCloud.DocumentDB.accounts.description: The body of a CyberCloud.DocumentDB/accounts. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the account is billed in.

backup.description: Backup to an object store, using CloudNativePG's barman-cloud. docs/plan/12: because it is PostgreSQL underneath, backup and point-in-time recovery are the operator's.

destinationPath.description: Object-store URL for base backups and WAL, for example s3://tenant-bucket/documentdb. Empty means no backup configuration is rendered, whatever enabled says.

enabled.description: Whether continuous backup and WAL archiving run. ⚠ Off by default, and only because there is no destination to default to: turning it on without a destinationPath below renders no backup configuration at all rather than an empty one, so the two properties have to be set together.

retentionDays.description: How long base backups and WAL are kept. The point-in-time-recovery window is this number of days.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose namespace holds the PostgreSQL cluster and the FerretDB gateway.

gateway.description: The FerretDB gateway — what speaks the MongoDB wire protocol.

replicas.description: Number of FerretDB pods. The gateway is stateless — it translates and forwards, and every byte is in PostgreSQL — so this is a throughput and availability setting rather than a topology one.

enabled.description: Whether both halves of this service are scraped: CloudNativePG is asked for a PodMonitor over the PostgreSQL pods, and the platform writes one over the FerretDB pods because FerretDB has no operator to ask. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production".

postgres.description: The CloudNativePG cluster the documents actually live in.

instances.description: Number of PostgreSQL instances, including the primary. One is a single point of failure and is offered for development only. Failover, replication and point-in-time recovery are CloudNativePG's, which is why this row costs 1.2 engineer-months rather than a rebuild of them.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per PostgreSQL instance, either by preset or explicitly. The FerretDB gateway pods are sized by the platform and are not affected.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Databases use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB.

storage.description: The data volume, per PostgreSQL instance.

class.description: StorageClass name for the PostgreSQL volumes. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: Data volume size per PostgreSQL instance, in Kubernetes quantity form. Every instance carries a full copy, so raw consumption is this times the instance count. Grows online; never shrinks.

version.description: FerretDB minor version. ⚠ One property moves two images: the DocumentDB PostgreSQL extension and the FerretDB gateway are released as a matched pair and a mismatched pair is a proxy talking to an extension it does not know. FerretDB maintains no long-term branch, so the two values here are the two most recent releases and a third is a new api-version.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

database.description: The database the DocumentDB extension is installed in, which is the one a driver authenticates against.

endpoint.description: The in-cluster MongoDB endpoint, mongodb://host:port/. ⚠ No external address is returned, because there is none — see the account's own documentation on exposure.

password.description: That role's password, read from the tenant's Vault for this call only.

username.description: The PostgreSQL role a client authenticates as. Not secret on its own; useless without the password below.

CyberCloud.Messaging.kafkaClusters.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Messaging/kafkaClusters. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the cluster is billed in.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose namespace holds the Strimzi objects.

cruiseControl.description: Cruise Control — partition rebalancing and broker-load reporting.

enabled.description: Whether Cruise Control runs. On by default: docs/plan/12 puts it in the chart rather than in a follow-up, because rebalancing a Kafka cluster by hand is the operational cost that makes this the most demanding service in the catalogue.

external.description: Exposure outside the cluster, via a load balancer and a firewall allow-list.

allowedCidrs.description: Source ranges permitted to reach the external listener. Required in substance rather than in schema: an empty list with external exposure on renders a load balancer that accepts nothing, which is the safe reading of an unfinished configuration.

enabled.description: Whether the cluster is reachable from outside the Kubernetes cluster. Off by default — docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions makes external exposure never the default, because a managed broker on a public IP with a weak password is the most common cloud breach there is.

listener.description: The in-cluster listener every client reaches.

tls.description: Whether the in-cluster listener requires TLS. On by default; turning it off is a plaintext broker on the pod network.

enabled.description: Whether the operator runs a Kafka Exporter alongside the cluster, exposing consumer-lag and topic metrics to the platform's metrics stack.

nodes.description: Number of Kafka nodes, each acting as both a KRaft controller and a broker. Use an odd number: a quorum of two tolerates no failures, and one is a single point of failure offered for development only.

retention.description: How long the cluster keeps messages by default. docs/plan/12 calls retention sizing an ongoing operational concern rather than a one-time setting.

hours.description: Default retention in hours. A week by default.

size.description: Default retention by partition size, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means retention is by time alone.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per node, either by preset or explicitly.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Brokers use the c1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 2 GiB and guaranteed rather than burstable.

class.description: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

deleteClaim.description: Whether deleting the resource also deletes the log volumes. Off by default, so a mistaken delete leaves the data recoverable by hand.

size.description: Log volume size per node, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

topics.description: Defaults applied to topics the cluster creates automatically. A topic created explicitly overrides them.

minInSyncReplicas.description: How many replicas must acknowledge a write before it is committed. Must be below the replication factor, or the cluster cannot tolerate one broker restart.

partitions.description: Default partition count for a new topic.

replicationFactor.description: Default replication factor for a new topic. Must not exceed the node count, or every produce to a new topic fails.

version.description: Apache Kafka version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window; a major upgrade is an explicit update to this field.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

bootstrapServers.description: The in-cluster bootstrap address, host:port. ⚠ The external listener's address is not returned here — an address a client cannot reach from where it is running is worse than an absent one.

password.description: The SCRAM user's password, read from the tenant's Vault for this call only.

CyberCloud.Messaging.natsClusters.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Messaging/natsClusters. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the cluster is billed in.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose namespace holds the NATS servers.

external.description: Exposure outside the cluster, via a load balancer and a firewall allow-list.

allowedCidrs.description: Source ranges permitted to reach the external listener. Required in substance rather than in schema: an empty list with external exposure on renders a load balancer that accepts nothing, which is the safe reading of an unfinished configuration.

enabled.description: Whether the cluster is reachable from outside the Kubernetes cluster. Off by default — docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions makes external exposure never the default, because a managed broker on a public IP with a weak password is the most common cloud breach there is.

jetstream.description: JetStream — the persistence layer streams and consumers live in. docs/plan/12 has it on unconditionally, so there is no switch to turn it off.

maxMemoryStore.description: Ceiling for memory-backed streams, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means no memory store at all, so every stream is file-backed — which is what docs/plan/12 asks for and what the volume above is sized for. A value here must leave room for the server itself inside the container's memory limit.

leafNodes.description: Leaf-node connectivity — docs/plan/12: "so a tenant's edge can attach".

enabled.description: Whether the servers accept leaf-node connections. Off by default: a leaf node joins the cluster's subject space, so it is a topology change rather than a client.

limits.description: Server limits a client can run into.

maxConnections.description: Largest number of client connections one server accepts.

maxPayload.description: Largest message a client may publish, in bytes. Raising it costs memory on every server, because a server buffers a whole message before routing it.

enabled.description: Whether a PodMonitor selects these servers' monitoring endpoint. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". The endpoint itself is always served; this decides whether anything scrapes it.

servers.description: Number of NATS servers. docs/plan/12 says three or five: JetStream replicates through a Raft group, so an even count buys no extra fault tolerance over the odd count below it. One is offered for development only and has no quorum at all.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per server, either by preset or explicitly.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Brokers use the c1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 2 GiB and guaranteed rather than burstable.

storage.description: The JetStream file store, per server.

class.description: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: JetStream file-store volume size per server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

version.description: NATS server version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window; a major upgrade is an explicit update to this field.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

monitoringUrl.description: The in-cluster HTTP monitoring endpoint, http://host:port — /varz and /jsz. Not secret, and returned here because a caller holding the client URL is the caller who needs it.

password.description: The client user's password, read from the tenant's Vault for this call only.

url.description: The in-cluster client URL, nats://host:port. ⚠ The external listener's address is not returned here — an address a client cannot reach from where it is running is worse than an absent one.

CyberCloud.Messaging.rabbitmqClusters.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Messaging/rabbitmqClusters. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the cluster is billed in.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose namespace holds the RabbitmqCluster.

limits.description: Broker limits a client can run into.

maxMessageSize.description: Largest message a client may publish, in bytes. Raising it costs memory on every node that holds a copy, which for a quorum queue is all of them.

nodes.description: Number of RabbitMQ nodes. Use an odd number of at least three: a quorum queue is a Raft group, so a group of two tolerates no failures and an even count buys nothing over the odd count below it. One is offered for development only and replicates nothing.

additional.description: Plugins to enable on top of the three the operator always enables — peer discovery, the management UI and the Prometheus endpoint. Each recognised plugin adds its own port to the cluster's in-cluster Service.

queues.description: How queues behave when a client does not say.

defaultType.description: The queue type a client gets when it declares a queue without asking for one. Quorum by default — docs/plan/12: a quorum queue is replicated through Raft across the nodes above, and on 4.x a classic queue is not replicated at all, so leaving this unset would put a single-node queue on a cluster the tenant paid three nodes for. This is a node-wide fallback: a vhost created with its own default queue type overrides it.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per node, either by preset or explicitly.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Brokers use the c1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 2 GiB and guaranteed rather than burstable.

class.description: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: Message-store volume size per node, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks. A quorum queue keeps its whole Raft log on every member, so this is the same figure on every node rather than a share of one.

version.description: RabbitMQ version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window; a major upgrade is an explicit update to this field. Only 4.x is offered: classic queue mirroring was removed in 4.0, so on every version here the replicated queue type is the quorum queue.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Messaging.rabbitmqClusters.title: CyberCloud.Messaging/rabbitmqClusters

CyberCloud.Messaging.rabbitmqClusters.Li.description: What CyberCloud.Messaging/rabbitmqClusters/listKeys returns. ⚠ Secret material. docs/plan/08 § The provider registry makes a secret action the only path a secret value leaves by; this schema is therefore the complete list of what does.

managementUrl.description: The in-cluster management UI and HTTP API, http://host:port. docs/plan/12 fronts this with the portal's authenticated proxy; it is never a public route.

password.description: The generated user's password, read from the cluster's default-user Secret for this call only. ⚠ Neither this value nor the user name is chosen by the platform: the operator generates both at first boot and RabbitMQ's own guest/guest account is never created.

url.description: The in-cluster AMQP URL, amqp://host:port. ⚠ There is no external address to return — this type declares no external listener at all, for the reason its schema gives.

CyberCloud.Network.virtualNetworks.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the virtual network lives in. ⚠ It selects which reserved ranges the address space is checked against — a region's underlay is part of that list.

addressSpace.description: The address range the network plans for. ⚠ Declarative: it is checked against the region's reserved ranges and is not rendered into the fabric, because a Kube-OVN Vpc carries no CIDR — the subnets do.

v4.description: The IPv4 range the network plans for, in CIDR form. It may overlap another of your own virtual networks — that is what a VPC is for — and it may not overlap a range the platform reserves, which is refused with the conflicting range named.

v6.description: The IPv6 range the network plans for, or empty for an IPv4-only network. ⚠ docs/plan/14 § IPv6 asks for dual-stack from day one rather than as a retrofit, which is why this is here at the first api-version even though a v4-only network is the ordinary case.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose fabric carries the network.

enableExternal.description: Whether the network's router is attached to the external network. Off by default: a network that reaches the outside without being asked is a network whose owner did not choose that. ⚠ Turning it on requires the cluster to have an external subnet configured; without one the Vpc is accepted and the attachment never completes.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Network.virtualNetworks.title: CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks

claim.description: What tenant isolation this network provides, in one sentence. It is the same sentence for every virtual network on the platform, and it is deliberately narrower than 'isolated'.

limits.description: What this network does NOT guarantee, one entry per limit, each naming the guarantee, why the substrate does not deliver it, and what to ask for instead. ⚠ Read this before deciding a virtual network satisfies a compliance requirement.

substrate.description: The technology enforcing the separation, named so that a tenant's own security review has something to review.

CyberCloud.Network.virtualNetworks.subne.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the subnet lives in. ⚠ It selects which reserved ranges the prefix is checked against, and it must be the network's own region — nothing checks that.

addressPrefix.description: The range addresses are allocated from.

v4.description: The IPv4 prefix, in CIDR form. ⚠ Host bits are cleared by the fabric, so 10.20.1.7/24 is stored as 10.20.1.0/24 and both name the same network. It may not overlap a range the platform reserves, which is refused with the conflicting range named.

v6.description: The IPv6 prefix, or empty for an IPv4-only subnet. Setting both makes the subnet dual-stack — docs/plan/14 § IPv6.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose fabric carries the subnet. Must be the cluster the network is in — nothing checks that, and a subnet placed elsewhere binds to a Vpc that does not exist there.

enableDhcp.description: Whether the fabric answers DHCP in this subnet. Off by default: an address is assigned to a workload's port when the port is created, and DHCP is for guests that insist on asking — a virtual machine rather than a container.

natOutgoing.description: Whether workloads in this subnet reach the internet through source NAT. Off by default. ⚠ This is the opposite of Kube-OVN's own default for its cluster subnet, deliberately: a tenant subnet that silently egresses is a surprise, and docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions defaults external exposure to off. It also requires the network's enableExternal to be on; without it the flag is accepted and nothing egresses.

private.description: Whether the subnet refuses traffic from other subnets. Off by default. ⚠ In this api-version it has no exception list, so on means no traffic from any other subnet in the network at all.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Network.virtualNetworks.subne.title: CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets

sampledAt.description: When the fabric last reported these figures, RFC 3339. ⚠ Returned because a count with no timestamp is a count a caller will read as live, and these come from the Subnet object's status rather than from a live query.

available.description: How many IPv4 addresses remain. ⚠ Zero here is the answer to 'why will nothing schedule in this subnet'.

total.description: How many IPv4 addresses the prefix contains that may be allocated, excluding the network address, the broadcast address and the gateway.

used.description: How many IPv4 addresses are currently allocated to ports.

available.description: How many IPv6 addresses remain, as a decimal string, or empty for an IPv4-only subnet.

total.description: How many IPv6 addresses the prefix contains, as a decimal string, or empty for an IPv4-only subnet. ⚠ A string because a /64 does not fit in the signed 64-bit integer SchemaKind.WholeNumber validates through.

CyberCloud.Search.services.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Search/services. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the service is billed in.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose namespace holds the search service.

coordinatingNodes.description: Number of coordinating-only nodes — nodes that hold no data and no cluster state and exist to fan a search out and merge the results. Zero is the default and is right until a query pattern makes one data node the bottleneck for every search. They are sized by the same preset as the data nodes.

dataNodes.description: Number of data nodes. This is the capacity axis: total raw capacity is this count times the disk size below, before replicas. Every data node also carries the ingest role, so an indexing pipeline needs no separate pool.

masterNodes.description: Number of dedicated cluster-manager nodes. They hold the cluster state in a quorum, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all. An even count is worse than the odd count below it and the API cannot say so — see the service's own documentation.

enabled.description: Whether the operator is asked for a ServiceMonitor. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ The metrics themselves come from the prometheus-exporter plugin, which the operator installs into every node on the first reconcile after this is turned on — so turning it on restarts the pods and turning it off does not remove the plugin.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per data node and per coordinating node, either by preset or explicitly. The cluster-manager nodes are sized by the platform and are not affected.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 8Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Search nodes use the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB, because OpenSearch is bound by heap and by the filesystem cache rather than by CPU. The m1 rungs below m1.small are deliberately not offered: OpenSearch derives its JVM heap from the container limit and a node under 4 GiB fails a bootstrap check after passing its readiness probe.

storage.description: The data volume, per data node.

class.description: StorageClass name for every node pool. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: Disk size per data node, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks. The cluster-manager and coordinating nodes get a fixed 10Gi that is not configurable and is counted against the storage quota anyway.

version.description: OpenSearch version. ⚠ OpenSearch is a fork of Elasticsearch 7.10 (ADR-011 — Elasticsearch is SSPL and is not available to us) and the two have diverged since, so an Elasticsearch 8 client is not promised anything here. Upgrades between the values below are online and in the maintenance window; a third value is a new api-version.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

endpoint.description: The in-cluster REST endpoint, https://host:port. ⚠ No external address is returned, because there is none — see the service's own documentation on exposure.

password.description: The administrative password, read from the tenant's Vault for this call only.

username.description: The administrative user. Always "admin": the operator generates exactly one credential and does not name it.

CyberCloud.Storage.accounts.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Storage/accounts. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the account is billed in.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose namespace holds the object store.

gateway.description: The S3 gateway — docs/plan/15's ADR-008: "the API is S3".

replicas.description: Number of S3 gateway pods. The gateway is stateless, so this is a throughput and availability setting rather than a topology one.

masters.description: Number of master servers. The masters hold the volume topology in a Raft group, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all.

enabled.description: Whether the operator is asked for a ServiceMonitor per component. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". Turning it off removes the metrics port as well as the scrape, which is the operator's own behaviour rather than this provider's.

replication.description: Where the second copy of every object is placed. None keeps one copy and is for scratch data only. A placement the cluster's topology cannot satisfy leaves volumes read-only rather than failing the create. Immutable, because SeaweedFS applies this to volumes as they are created and never rewrites the ones that already exist — a change would split the account into two durability promises with no way to tell which object got which.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per volume server, either by preset or explicitly. The masters, the filer and the S3 gateway are sized by the platform and are not affected.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Volume servers use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB.

storage.description: The data volume, per volume server.

class.description: StorageClass name for the volume servers. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: Data volume size per volume server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

version.description: SeaweedFS version. ⚠ SeaweedFS ships a release roughly weekly and maintains no long-term branch, so docs/plan/12's "supported major versions" is a shape this project does not have; the two values here are the two most recent releases and a new api-version is what adds a third.

volumeServers.description: Number of volume servers. This is the capacity axis: total raw capacity is this count times the volume size below, before replication.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Storage.accounts.title: CyberCloud.Storage/accounts

CyberCloud.Storage.accounts.ListKeysResp.description: What CyberCloud.Storage/accounts/listKeys returns. ⚠ Secret material. docs/plan/08 § The provider registry makes a secret action the only path a secret value leaves by; this schema is therefore the complete list of what does.

accessKeyId.description: The access key id. Not secret on its own; useless without the pair below.

endpoint.description: The in-cluster S3 endpoint, http://host:port. ⚠ No external address is returned, because there is none — see the account's own documentation on exposure.

region.description: The region name an S3 client signs with. SeaweedFS does not route on it, and SigV4 refuses to sign without one, so it is returned rather than left for the caller to guess.

secretAccessKey.description: The secret access key, read from the tenant's Vault for this call only.

CyberCloud.Storage.accounts.buckets.description: The body of a CyberCloud.Storage/accounts/buckets. Generated from the provider registry's schema, which is the same object the write path validates against — docs/plan/08 § The provider registry.

location.description: The region the bucket is billed in.

clusterId.description: The cluster whose namespace holds the bucket. Must be the cluster the account is in — nothing checks that, and a bucket placed elsewhere is applied into a namespace with no object store in it.

quota.description: How much the bucket may hold.

size.description: The bucket's size limit, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means no limit other than the account's own provisioned capacity. ⚠ This is a limit inside capacity the account already reserved; it does not add any, and it is not what the bucket is billed on.

versioning.description: Whether the bucket keeps previous versions of an overwritten object. Off by default. ⚠ docs/plan/15 § Object storage: SeaweedFS' S3 implementation is "good but not complete" and names object versioning as one of the partial areas, so the supported-operations table for the deployed version — not this property — is what says how completely it behaves.

tags.description: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Storage.accounts.buckets.title: CyberCloud.Storage/accounts/buckets

objectCount.description: How many objects the bucket holds, as of the last sample.

sampledAt.description: When the two figures above were sampled, RFC 3339. ⚠ Returned because a sampled number with no timestamp is a number a caller will read as live.

sizeBytes.description: How many bytes the bucket holds before replication, as of the last sample. ⚠ Sampled rather than live — docs/plan/15 § Metering samples SeaweedFS volume stats hourly per bucket — so it is not a number to write an assertion against immediately after a PUT.

details.description: Every other problem found. A form that has to be fixed one field per round trip is a form nobody finishes.

message.description: For a human, naming the actual numbers. 'Quota exceeded' without the meter, the request and the remainder is a support ticket by construction.

target.description: An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the request body, so the portal can highlight the field.

ErrorCode.description: A stable, documented, greppable identifier. ⚠ It is part of the API contract and changing one is a breaking change — docs/plan/08 § Errors. The closed set is CyberCloud.Core.ErrorCode.All.

ErrorResponse.description: One shape, everywhere, Azure's. docs/plan/08 § Errors.

OperationProgress.description: One progress entry. The array is this platform's addition to Azure's pattern and is what makes a nine-minute cluster creation tolerable — docs/plan/10.

message.description: What happened, naming the actual numbers.

step.description: The phase a reconciler reported — applying, waiting-for-ready.

OperationState.description: Azure's status vocabulary. ⚠ Canceled is reached only after the delete path has run for everything already applied — cancellation completes rather than abandoning.

OperationStatus.description: An operation's current state. ⚠ The members are docs/plan/10 § Long-running operations, over HTTP's, which is a subset of the OperationStatus wire type — no HTTP projection of that record is declared anywhere in the tree.
